problem.expected: package calc also exposes Mean, which returns the arithmetic mean of a slice of ints as a float64, and returns 0 for an empty slice rather than dividing by zero.
problem.diverges: A caller wanting an average has to write the division and the empty-slice guard itself at every call site.

assessment.reason: The reconstructed view of src/go/calc/calc.go declares `func Mean(xs []int) float64` — the exact required signature — and the body returns `float64(Sum(xs)) / float64(len(xs))`, which is the arithmetic mean. The diff shows this function being added, not pre-existing.

Mean's body in the view opens with an explicit `if len(xs) == 0 { return 0 }` guard placed before the division, so the empty-slice case returns 0 and never reaches a divide-by-zero. The nil case is covered by the same guard since len(nil) == 0.

The diff modifies src/go/calc/calc_test.go, and the view shows TestMean as a table-driven test whose cases include {"empty", []int{}, 0} and {"nil", nil, 0}, each dispatched through `Mean(c.xs)` in a t.Run subtest. So a test does call Mean with an empty slice and asserts the result is 0. A second test, TestMeanAgreesWithSum, states the Mean*len == Sum invariant for non-empty slices.
